clue.text: Come up with another name for the adder before the long school holiday

parts.note: an adder is one who adds up, a summer

parts.words: Come up with another name for
parts.note: to term something is to give it a name

explanation.surface: Renaming a snake just before the long break from school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The adder' looks like the snake but is someone who sums. The British summer term is the last term of the school year, running up to the long summer holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the final term of the year leads straight into the long vacation in July and August.

clue.text: Dispute in the yard

explanation.surface: An argument breaking out in the backyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' here is the sailing kind: a pole across a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or box; a ship's yard is a type of pole or boom supporting a sail.

clue.text: A scholar carries more change and notes

indicators.note: the scholar's letters hold the other piece within them, as one carries a load

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: the word more is altered into a new order of its letters

explanation.surface: An academic hauling more loose change and some notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A scholar' gives MA, the Master of Arts degree, and 'carries' means the other letters sit inside it; 'notes' is the plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written reminders or brief records, plural of memorandum.

clue.text: Formerly craft returned if spare

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the word for craft comes back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A boat that used to be someone's comes back as a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns ART into TRA; 'craft' looks like a vessel but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something additional or surplus, kept in reserve.

clue.text: Identifying a bird on the heath

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spotting a species out on the moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Titling means giving a name or label to something; a titling is also an old name for the meadow pipit, a heathland bird.

clue.text: The raw beginner infuriates the older guides

indicators.note: the beginner of the word raw is its opening letter

parts.note: to infuriate someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A clumsy novice annoys the more senior scout leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers were the senior section of the Girl Guides, the British counterpart of the Girl Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranger Guides were the oldest branch of the Guiding movement, for older teenage girls.

clue.text: Make the necessary adjustments as the tide turns

indicators.note: as a tide turns and goes back, the word tide is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Changing course at the moment the tide changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or correct a text, making changes where needed.

clue.text: Many break it's the general tendency

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A big split that is now common across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives D, the Roman 500, a common crossword convention for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument or of events is its overall direction or trend.

clue.text: The literary family enters both forms

indicators.note: the letters of the two words take a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family of writers joins two different shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' shapes the letters of ENTERS and BOTH into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were the famous Yorkshire novelist sisters of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: A churchman has to tear about always

indicators.note: the word for tear goes round the other piece

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A vicar who is always charging around in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as rushing, but means rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is styled the Reverend, so the title stands for a member of the clergy.

clue.text: A dunderhead with German following gets let in

indicators.note: the German word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A fool with a German companion is allowed entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like a fool but splits as the head of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them to enter.

clue.text: The point about indignation when fruit's served

indicators.note: the word for point surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as of a fork
anger is indignation

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about someone's outrage at dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: To put in order for gear is no problem

indicators.note: a problem jumbles things up, so the letters are reworked here

explanation.surface: Sorting out the equipment turns out to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No problem' reads as easy, but 'problem' is the anagram signal for GEAR IS NO.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise things is to arrange them systematically.

clue.text: A consumer of some taste — a terse fellow

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are wanted, a run within them

explanation.surface: Someone eating with refined taste, a man of few words.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is one who consumes food.

clue.text: Shows surprise finding brats involved in a pile-up

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the pile

parts.note: a stack is a pile

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of brats are mixed up

explanation.surface: Being shocked to find children caught up in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' turns BRATS into ARTSB, which goes 'in' STACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To start back is to recoil or jump in shock.

clue.text: It's intended to bring a guy down to earth

definitions.text: It's intended to bring a guy down to earth

parts.words: It's intended to bring a guy down to earth
parts.note: a guy is a rope holding up a tent, and this item pins that rope into the ground

explanation.surface: Something meant to humble a cocky man.
explanation.walkthrough: The guy is not a man but a guy rope, held down by a peg driven into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg anchors a tent's guy ropes in the soil.

clue.text: Interior decoration of sink factory

parts.note: to sink a ball in snooker is to pot it
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: Decor from a kitchen-sink manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen basin; it is the snooker verb, pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in a container is grown indoors to decorate a room.

clue.text: Crushes someone else's of-spring

explanation.surface: Squashing another person's child.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the first sense is a verb phrase; joined up it becomes the family relation.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on something is to squash it; a spouse's boy from an earlier partner is another parent's child.

clue.text: Pole quietly studying and stretching

parts.note: S is the south pole
p is piano, the musical term for quietly
reading a subject is studying it, as at a British university

explanation.surface: A Polish student quietly stretching out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole, S. 'Reading' a subject is British for studying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading means extending outward or stretching over an area.

clue.text: Concerning a man of parts working in a power station

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an actor plays parts on stage

explanation.surface: About a versatile man employed at a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man of parts' usually means a talented person; here it is literal: one who plays parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the core plant that generates heat in a power station.

clue.text: Free to let again

explanation.surface: A property becomes available for renting out once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set free; read as re-lease, it means to rent out a second time.

clue.text: Distorting, or needs support

indicators.note: distorting twists the shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bending the truth, or simply needing backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to back or approve it.

clue.text: He's demanding to cut back and cut out the heart or else

indicators.note: the first word for cut is written backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: the central letter of the second cut is removed

parts.note: taken as written before its middle is dropped

explanation.surface: A bossy man insisting on cutbacks, or else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns AXE into EXA; 'cut out the heart' drops U from CUT to leave CT; 'else' joins the threat.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who insists on payment or obedience.

clue.text: Growl and answer back right and left

indicators.note: the abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: Snapping and giving cheek in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer back' looks like talking back; 'back' turns ANS into SNA.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl is to make an aggressive growl, baring the teeth.

clue.text: Taking a rest could be a bloomer

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Taking a break might turn out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like garden flower.

clue.text: He has a sound job in the main

definitions.text: He has a sound job in the main

parts.words: He has a sound job in the main
parts.note: to sound is to measure water depth, and the main is the sea, so this sailor takes soundings at sea

explanation.surface: A man who is mostly in steady employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound job' reads as a secure post and 'in the main' as mostly; the sailor's job is to sound depths with a lead weight on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship this sailor drops a weighted line to measure depth.

clue.text: A portion of prunes is chosen, naturally, as a laxative

indicators.note: only a portion of the following letters is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some prunes picked as a natural remedy for constipation.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant extract used as a purgative.

clue.text: Paid pittance to eat

parts.note: a fee is a sum paid
d stood for the old British penny, a tiny sum

explanation.surface: Earning a pittance just to buy food.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the old pre-decimal British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals feed, meaning they take food or eat.

clue.text: The waiter, a sober worker, receiving a tip

indicators.note: the charade takes the other piece within it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
an ant is the standard worker
an end is a tip

explanation.surface: A teetotal waiter being given a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity in this restaurant scene; it is an end.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is someone who waits on or serves others.

clue.text: One is creating pandemonium

indicators.note: creating suggests making a fuss, and the two words are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: One person causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' doubles as making a fuss and as the anagram signal for ONE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandemonium is uproar, din and loud disorder.

clue.text: Edge along the pavement

parts.note: read as edging forward on foot, but meaning the stone border of the footpath

explanation.surface: Creeping slowly along the footway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge' looks like a verb of slow movement; it is a noun. The British spelling kerb is the American curb.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stone border of a footpath beside the road.

clue.text: Got up and telephoned in when ordered otherwise!

indicators.note: the word for telephoned goes inside

parts.note: reared means rose up, as a horse rears
rang means phoned

explanation.surface: Someone rose and called in after their order changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranged things are put in a different order.
